rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault (Not-At-Fault) Evictions under RSO & JCO
rules.requirement: Landlords in Los Angeles must pay relocation assistance and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before evicting a tenant for any no-fault reason (owner/family occupancy, demolition, condo conversion, government order to vacate, etc.) under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance. Payment amounts vary by tenant eligibility status, length of tenancy, and income, and must be made within 15 days of the termination notice.
rules.key_value: Relocation payments ranging from $11,000 to $27,400 (or one month's rent for certain single-family dwellings), effective July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) in the City of Los Angeles where the landlord terminates tenancy for a no-fault reason.
rules.exemptions: Exempt when evicting a resident manager to replace with another manager (unless a Manager-Tenant), when eviction is due to natural disaster hazards not caused by landlord negligence, and reduced 'Mom and Pop' amounts apply for small (4-or-fewer-unit) owner-occupied buildings under specified conditions.
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the tenant is 'eligible' or 'qualified' (age, disability, dependents) and whether the tenant is low-income, which affect the relocation amount owed; whether the property is a single-family dwelling owned by a natural person owning 4 or fewer units.

rules.conflict_note: Dollar amounts shown are for the period July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 and increase annually each July 1st.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO) - Relocation for Demolition of Protected Units for New Construction
rules.requirement: When a landlord terminates tenancy to demolish a 'Protected Unit' for new construction, enhanced relocation assistance and occupant protections (right to return, right of first refusal, 6-month notice) apply for lower-income tenants, consistent with the state Housing Crisis Act, whichever amount is higher.
rules.key_value: Enhanced relocation payments per Chart B for low/very low/extremely low income households, plus occupant protections (6-month notice, right to return, right of first refusal); penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit for noncompliance
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to 'Protected Units' (RSO units, rent-restricted units, or units rented by lower/very low income households within the past 5 years, or units withdrawn under the Ellis Act within 10 years) being demolished for new construction in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions: Regular RSO or JCO relocation rules (not RPO) apply if the units to be demolished are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant.
rules.quoted_span: which must be enhanced for lower income tenants if the project is subject to the Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO), effective 2/11/2025 under Ordinances # 188481 and #188482.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the unit qualifies as a 'Protected Unit' (rent-restricted, subject to rent control, or rented by lower-income households within past 5 years, or Ellis-withdrawn within 10 years) and whether the tenant is lower-income (80% AMI or below).

rules.conflict_note: RSO and JCO amounts must also be enhanced for lower income tenants under the state Housing Crisis Act regardless of RPO applicability; the City requires payment of whichever of the two (state HCA or city RPO) is higher.
